title: Mediterranean-Inspired 7-Layer Dip
description: Layered dips are usually the life‑of‑the‑party comfort food, and this riff swaps the usual Tex‑Mex suspects for Mediterranean flavors, mostly from your pantry. What makes this dip irresistible isn’t just the balance of of all the different flavors in the layers, it’s the presentation. Built in a wide platter or dish (not a deep bowl), each layer is proudly on display, practically begging for pita chips to dive straight down and grab a bit of everything in one swipe. Serve it as an appetizer for a meze spread, an easy make‑ahead option for potlucks or tailgates, or the centerpiece of a snack‑for‑dinner night with chilled rosé. One look at the stripes of color and texture, and guests will know they’re in for more than your average dip.
ingredients: 2 (15.5-ounce) cans cannellini or great northern beans
4 teaspoons freshly squeezed lemon juice, divided
1/4 teaspoon freshly cracked black pepper, divided
1 (16-ounce) package labneh (about 1 1/2 cups), such as Cedar’s
1/3 cup toasted chopped walnuts plus 2 tablespoons, divided
3 tablespoons finely chopped herbs, such as mint, dill or parsley, divided
1/8 teaspoon Aleppo or red chili flakes
3/4 cup cherry tomatoes, in small bits
1/4 cup thinly sliced and cup up red onion or pickled red onion
Serve with warm pita bread or chips, carrots, cucumber, celery and bell pepper and lemon
directions: Drain the beans and reserve 1/4 cup of liquid. Rinse beans.

Combine beans, 1/4 cup reserved bean liquid, pesto, tahini, lemon juice, 1 small garlic clove, 1/4 teaspoon salt, 1/4 teaspoon salt and 1/8 teaspoon black pepper, in a food processor, process on HIGH, until just smooth, about 45 seconds. Spread this mixture as a base layer on a platter.

Stir together labneh, 1/3 cup walnuts, cucumber, 2 tablespoons herbs, Aleppo (red chile flakes) and remaining 1/4 teaspoon salt and 1/8 teaspoon pepper until just combined. Finely grate with a microplane the remaining 1 small garlic clove. Spread this mixture gently on top of the bean layer, allowing 1/2 inch of the bean layer to show.
Sprinkle on the remaining layers on top of the creamy layer starting with cherry tomatoes, onion, feta, olives, and remaining 2 tablespoons walnuts.
Garnish with olive oil, additional smoked paprika and serve with pita, chips, cucumber, celery, bell peppers and lemon wedges.
Note: To make labneh from scratch, whisk 1/2 teaspoon salt into 2 cups whole-milk plain yogurt, bundle in cheesecloth over a bowl, refrigerate 12 to 24 hours, then unwrap and serve.
